newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X deadline approaches without comment.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X deadline approaches without comment.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd was silent again Friday as the clock ticked on a November 22 deadline to take steps to settle an ownership dispute.
Bre-X partner PT Krueng Gasui had given Bre-X until today to take steps to resolve their dispute over the rich Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
Krueng Gasui, which is claiming up to 40 percent of the rich Busang deposit, has said it will sue Bre-X for US$1.9 billion in Canadian courts if no steps are taken.
Bre-X has said it was willing to talk with Krueng Gasui, but would not say Friday whether it had made attempts yet.
The company maintained its month-long silence, communicating with the public only through occasional technical and complicated news releases.
Bre-X's lawyer in Calgary would not comment either.
In Indonesia on Friday, Jusuf Merukh, which controls Krueng Gasui, reiterated his threat.
"Bre-X has until November 22 Canadian time to agree to a meeting and negotiations ... failing which I will file the suit in Canada," he told Reuters.
A second threat of a lawsuit surfaced Friday from the previous owners of a small section of the Busang discovery.

The previous owners, Waverly Mining Finance Plc, Montague Gold NL, Westralian Resource Projects Ltd and William McLucas, threatened legal action unless they were included in the negotiations with Krueng Gasui. They said their claims against Bre-X "mirror" Krueng Gasui's claims.
Bre-X called the threats "entirely without foundation."
Most analysts threw up their hands in despair.

"I'm just so uncertain as to what may be true or untrue, so I'm standing aside and letting this thing unfold," said one analyst. "This happens with every major discovery, there's always someone who will come out of the woodwork."
Even if the claims have no merit, they cause costly delays and usually end in the complainants winning a cash settlement to go away, he added.
"It's just more uncertainty thrown into the pot," said gold analyst Michael Jalonen of Midland-Walwyn. "There's just so much backroom intrigue right now."
Bre-X shares closed up C$0.20 at C$23.90 on the Toronto Stock Exchange, with 1.8 million shares trading hands.

The ownership dispute prompted Indonesian government officials to delay issuing Bre-X its necessary permits, but a recent change in powers within the mining ministry and news that the government is processing a batch of permits has prompted speculation that Bre-X's permits may be issued soon.
